Karthik / team — adding concrete ops guidance Tom asked for. Pasting the short-runbook + snippets below. I’ll also drop a markdown doc into the Drive folder.

1) Auth / keys- Use standard Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>. Issue a scoped key limited to staging.acme-retail.com with read/write scopes appropriate for POC. Rotate keys every 90 days for production; implement a key-vault for staging as well. Consider short-lived session tokens if you need per-user isolation.

2) Routing / region selection- For low latency pick the region param (region=us-west) in SDK config; Redwood will route to the closest provisioned pool. For higher availability configure fallback region=us-east in the SDK so requests automatically failover if primary returns 5xx or is overloaded.

3) Structured output / tool calling- If you expect tool calls or structured JSON responses, use the SDK's streaming parser and include a response schema to detect truncated output. On truncated responses (stream cut due to token limits) we recommend returning a partial result + continuation token that your service can replay to fetch the remainder.

4) Embeddings vs. reranker guidance- Embeddings: good for approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search; reranker: lightweight cross-encoder on top of candidate set for higher precision. For 200 RPS, run candidate retrieval by ANN (Faiss/HNSW) and call reranker at 10-20 RPS (sampled) unless you budget for full-rerank. Cache embedding vectors per SKU to avoid re-embedding on each request.

5) Rate limiting, retries, 429 handling- Client-side: token bucket limiter tuned to your steady RPS + burst capacity. Server-side: Redwood enforces per-key quotas and will return 429 when quota exceeded.

Recommended retry/backoff policy (start here):
- Idempotent reads (GET/generation with deterministic request-id): retry with exponential backoff + full jitter.
- Base backoff: 150ms; multiplier: 2x; cap: 8s; max attempts: 6.
- For 429 specifically: respect Retry-After header if present, otherwise use backoff above.

6) Idempotency & request IDs- Attach both X-Request-Id (opaque correlation id) and Idempotency-Key for operations that create/modify server state. Store idempotency keys server-side for at least 24 hours (48 hours recommended for cross-region retries). If the operation is non-idempotent (charged billing/event dedupe) require a client-supplied Idempotency-Key.

7) Observability- Emit traces with the correlation header; log request size, model, token counts, and latency buckets. Redwood Console will surface token-level breakdowns if you include the SDK metadata header (X-RW-Meta: {env:staging,team:search}).

Attachments: 429-retry-playbook.md (will be added to Drive)
